title: Exit Optionality
equation: Business Value = Profit × Transferability × Founder Independence
hook: If the business falls apart the week you take a vacation, you own a job, not a company.
statement: Build your company so it could be sold, even if you never plan to sell it.
explainer: Building something sellable forces cleaner systems, stronger people, and more freedom for you. Even if you keep it forever, you end up owning an asset instead of just an income.
sop: Ask what would make your company attractive to a buyer.
Hand off the tasks only you can do right now.
Score Profit, Transferability, and Founder Independence from 1 to 10.
Review how sellable it is once a year.
equation_example: Profit 7, Transferability 4, Founder Independence 3. 7 × 4 × 3 = 84 Business Value, out of 1,000. Higher means a buyer could step in and it keeps running. Lower means it's really a job dressed up as a company.
question: Write down one thing that would make your business valuable without you holding it together.
closing_statement: Build an asset, not just an income.
caption:
Principle Nº 252: Exit Optionality

If the business falls apart the week you take a vacation, you own a job, not a company.

Build your company so it could be sold, even if you never plan to sell it.

Your turn: Write down one thing that would make your business valuable without you holding it together.
